review_findings.description: The applied PR spliced the nonce property into the middleware call signature and declared the helper inside getHeaderValue, leaving the TypeScript source syntactically invalid.
nonce() generated the random nonce when the helper was created, so a nonce function configured once at app startup would reuse the same CSP nonce across requests.

The helper trusted any existing res.locals.cspNonce string and embedded it in the CSP header without nonce-character validation, allowing malformed or injected source expressions if that value was attacker influenced.

blue_fix.fix_explanation: Moved the nonce helper to module scope and attached it correctly to contentSecurityPolicy. The returned directive-value function now generates a fresh 128-bit base64url nonce at request time, stores it on res.locals.cspNonce, reuses an already generated per-request nonce only when it has valid base64url characters, and returns the quoted nonce source expression. Added a regression test covering the app-startup CSP directive usage so nonce values differ across requests.
